scope: App/server, database and Worker namespace isolation plus publishing UI recovery
correctedDuringReview: Standalone legacy Pages redirect still accepted QA labels.
Failed or malformed status refresh retained prior UI permission.
Saved preparation metadata could lock an unavailable old address after namespace cutover.
Out-of-order refreshes could overwrite newer state; mutation start and settlement now invalidate older reads.
Uncertain writes retained preflight confidence; explicit status refresh now required before discarding the saved request.

implementation.serverGuard: Server-only mode and QA workspace; exact staging DB required. Browser flags are not authority.
implementation.sqlGuard: Private owner configuration plus triggers on sites, reservations and preparations; production default reserves QA labels; conflicting prior ownership aborts.
implementation.workerGuard: Exact staging routes and pinned bindings; production QA exclusion before cache/forms/redirect/RPC; namespace cache partition.
implementation.compatibility: Existing ordinary sites retain reads and reduction/cleanup operations. No sites or ownership rewritten. Hostname syntax remains independent.

limitations: Live staging still uses the historical app/database/Worker; exact DNS/TLS/routes/bindings need coordinated cutover and observation.
A new staging cutover must stop if an unguarded production fallback is present; this package never authorizes production changes.
Actual remote publication executor, immutable images, lifecycle journal/host and scoped cloud credentials remain unqualified.
Required plan switching, real payment lifecycle/credit packs and fresh generated output quality remain open.
OpenAI key is absent; required live image qualification remains open.
Candidate inventory remains unfrozen until coordinated release review; local tests do not establish competitive superiority.
